recap_session: Thu Jul 3 (early close) / Wed Jul 2 last full session
headline: Post-holiday futures open higher as a soft June jobs report cools rate-hike expectations, SpaceX joins the Nasdaq-100 today triggering forced passive buying, and oil slides on OPEC+ supply increases and easing Strait of Hormuz tensions.
stance: Cautiously constructive. The first post-Independence Day session reopens with tech futures leading — Nasdaq-100 futures up ~1.1% overnight — propelled by a weak NFP print that dialed back September rate-hike odds from ~67% to ~50%. The dollar (DXY) is holding below 101, a tailwind for gold and risk assets. The week's big risk is Wednesday's FOMC minutes: the June dot plot showed half of voting members penciling in at least one hike, and Chair Warsh's hawkish reputation means markets will read every word carefully. Positioning remains a contrarian support — speculators are near 3-year short extremes in Nasdaq-100 and Russell 2000 futures, meaning any sustained rally could force short-covering.

news.head: SpaceX joins Nasdaq-100 today
news.body: SPCX is added to the Nasdaq-100 effective today (Jul 6), with tracker funds — including QQQ — estimated to buy roughly $4.3 billion in SPCX shares today alone, and total passive rebalancing across all Nasdaq-100 and linked index funds potentially reaching ~$27 billion; the stock has only ~3–5% of shares freely available to trade, creating a very tight supply-demand dynamic.

news.head: June NFP: 57K, far below 110K forecast
news.body: The US economy added just 57,000 jobs in June — the smallest gain in four months and well below the 110,000 consensus — driving markets to cut the implied probability of a September Fed rate hike from ~67% to ~50%; the unemployment rate held at 4.2%, though the drop partly reflected a shrinking labor force.

news.head: FOMC minutes due Wednesday
news.body: The Federal Reserve publishes its June meeting minutes Wednesday at 2 p.m. ET; during that meeting roughly half of voting members indicated they expected at least one rate increase before year-end, and with Chair Kevin Warsh seen as favoring tighter policy, the market will scrutinize the document closely for the next policy pivot.

news.head: Iran ceasefire holds; OPEC+ opens taps
news.body: Iran's week of state mourning for Supreme Leader Khamenei continued over the weekend without major escalation, and OPEC+ agreed to a modest output increase from August; oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz are recovering, with Brent trading at an overnight level of ~$71.88 and WTI near ~$68.58.

news.head: Dollar at multi-week low
news.body: The DXY dollar index is holding below 101 overnight after its largest weekly decline since April, dragged lower by the soft NFP and reduced rate-hike expectations; a weaker dollar supports gold, commodities priced in dollars, and US multinationals.

news.head: TSMC June revenue due Friday
news.body: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) reports June monthly revenue on Friday July 10, serving as a live bellwether for the entire US semiconductor and AI sector ahead of Q2 earnings season.

news.head: SpaceX analyst quiet period ends
news.body: The mandatory post-IPO analyst quiet period for SpaceX expires this week, meaning Wall Street research firms can now publish their first formal ratings and price targets — adding a new price-discovery catalyst on top of today's index inclusion.

implications: The soft June jobs print is a double-edged sword: it lowers the near-term hike bar (equity-friendly) but also signals genuine labor market cooling at a moment when real rates sit at 2.26% — a level that is still a headwind for expensive growth stocks (S&P CAPE: 41.6x).

SpaceX's Nasdaq-100 inclusion creates a mechanical, time-sensitive buy event today: with only 3–5% of shares in free float and an estimated $4–27 billion in forced passive demand, SPCX could see extreme intraday price action that also reshuffles weights across other Nasdaq-100 members.
Wednesday's FOMC minutes are the week's highest-risk event: a hawkish tone (50% of members leaning toward a hike) could reverse the post-NFP rate-cut optimism and reprice both bonds and equities.
Oil's softness (WTI overnight ~$68.58, 35th percentile over 3 years) is good for inflation expectations (10-year breakeven: 2.23%) and airline/consumer stocks, but is a headwind for energy names.

Positioning: Speculators are near 3-year short extremes (extended short) in Nasdaq-100 futures (1st percentile), Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile), and 3M SOFR (1st percentile) — a contrarian floor that means speculators have almost no bullish bets left in those markets, historically a setup where any positive catalyst can accelerate a short-covering rally. In copper, speculators are heavily positioned long (95th percentile) — a contrarian warning. British pound specs are also at a 3-year extended short (1st percentile), a contrarian-bullish lean for sterling.

watch.head: SPCX intraday liquidity crunch
watch.body: Watch SpaceX (SPCX) for extreme intraday moves as passive funds are forced to absorb shares in a thin float; sharp SPCX volatility could ripple into other large Nasdaq-100 weights as indices rebalance.

watch.head: 10-year Treasury yield direction
watch.body: The 10-year yield closed at 4.49% (prior cash close Jul 2); a further drift lower would confirm the market is repricing the hike path, supporting equities — a move back above 4.55% would be a warning shot.

watch.head: DXY holds below 101
watch.body: If the dollar index (overnight ~100.88) continues to soften, that sustains the tailwind for gold (currently above $4,100 overnight), copper, and emerging-market assets; a surprise bounce back above 101.5 would pressure the reflation trade.

watch.head: USD/JPY at 97.9th-pctile extreme
watch.body: The Japanese yen stands at 161.34 per dollar (prior close Jul 3) — a 3-year extreme — raising the risk of Bank of Japan intervention; any sudden yen strengthening would unwind carry trades and could spike volatility across risk assets globally.

watch.head: Oil/Hormuz headlines
watch.body: With the ceasefire fragile and Iran's mourning period ongoing, any fresh Strait of Hormuz headline could rapidly reprice oil (Brent overnight ~$71.88) and re-inject geopolitical risk premium into broader markets.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: June payrolls came in at just 57K (prior cash data) vs. a 110K forecast — the weakest print in four months — pushing implied odds of a September Fed rate hike down from ~67% to ~50%.

The 10-year Treasury yield sits at 4.49% (prior cash close Jul 2) and the 2-year at 4.14%, keeping the yield curve at a modest +35 bps spread — steeper curves typically signal improving growth expectations.
Real interest rates (the inflation-adjusted rate) remain at 2.26% (as of Jul 2), still historically high and a structural drag on long-duration assets like expensive tech stocks.
The 10-year inflation breakeven (the market's guess for future inflation) stands at 2.23% (Jul 2) — contained, and drifting lower post-NFP, consistent with Fed rate-hike odds pulling back.
The DXY dollar index is holding below 101 overnight after its biggest weekly drop since April, as softer labor data reduces the case for near-term tightening.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh noted inflation expectations are moderating while reaffirming the Fed's commitment to price stability — a carefully balanced message that keeps both hike and hold scenarios alive.

Wednesday's FOMC minutes (2 p.m. ET) are the week's primary macro event: the June dot plot showed ~50% of members expected a hike this year, and any hawkish nuance in the minutes could reverse the post-NFP rally.
Bank reserves stand at $2,967 billion (Jul 1) and the Treasury's cash account (TGA) at $880 billion — system liquidity remains ample, a backstop for credit markets.

Financial conditions indexes (ANFCI -0.49, STLFSI -0.64 as of Jun 26) both show easier-than-normal conditions — meaning credit is flowing freely and borrowing costs are below their historical average relative to the economy.
sections.positioning: Speculators are near a 3-year extended short in 3M SOFR futures (1st percentile) — speculators have almost no bullish bets left, a contrarian floor suggesting rate-futures markets are priced for the worst and any dovish pivot could trigger a sharp reversal.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500 prior cash close (Jul 2): 7,483.24; overnight futures (pre-market, ~6 a.m. ET): +0.5% — pointing to a gap-up open back toward the week's highs.
Nasdaq-100 prior cash close (Jul 2): 25,832.67; overnight futures: +1.1% — tech is leading the post-holiday bounce, driven by AI/semi tailwinds and SpaceX index-inclusion flows.
Dow Jones prior cash close (Jul 2): 52,900.07; Dow futures overnight are near flat, lagging tech — consistent with the rotation into growth names.

SpaceX (SPCX) officially joins the Nasdaq-100 before tomorrow's open (Jul 7), meaning passive fund managers must execute the bulk of their forced buying today (Jul 6); QQQ alone may need to purchase ~$4.3 billion in SPCX with only ~3–5% of shares freely available — expect elevated volatility in SPCX and ripple effects in other large Nasdaq-100 weights.
Market breadth remains healthy: 66.9% of S&P 500 stocks and 65.3% of Nasdaq-100 stocks are trading above their 200-day moving average (as of Jul 2) — a broad, not just mega-cap, rally.

The CAPE ratio (a smoothed long-term valuation measure) stands at 41.6x (Jul 2) — historically elevated, meaning the market is pricing in strong future earnings growth with little margin for disappointment.

The equity risk premium — the extra return stocks offer over bonds — sits at -2.05% (Jun 30): bonds are actually offering more expected return than stocks on a risk-adjusted basis, a valuation warning for buy-and-hold equity investors.

VIX (the S&P 500's 30-day fear gauge) closed at 15.81 (Jul 3), comfortably low — markets are not pricing significant near-term turbulence, though the SKEW index at 150 suggests options traders are paying up for tail-risk protection against a large sudden drop.
TSM (Taiwan Semiconductor) June revenue data due Friday July 10 — widely watched as a real-time read on AI chip demand ahead of the full Q2 earnings season.

Asia overnight: mostly positive — Hong Kong Hang Seng +0.4%, Jakarta +2.28%, but Japan's Nikkei -0.95% (a reminder that USD/JPY at extreme 161.34 level creates yen-volatility risk); Europe's Stoxx 600 near record highs.
sections.positioning: Speculators are near 3-year extended short extremes in Nasdaq-100 futures (1st percentile) and Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile) — speculators have almost no bullish bets left in these markets, a historically contrarian floor. VIX futures specs are also lightly short (12th percentile). A sustained rally could force aggressive short-covering, amplifying upside moves.

single_name.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.
single_name.catalyst: June monthly revenue report due Friday July 10; widely watched as a real-time bellwether for AI chip demand ahead of Q2 earnings season.
single_name.note: Any revenue beat or raised guidance would likely lift the broader semiconductor complex; a miss could pressure AI-exposed names across the Nasdaq-100.
